claims.text: The rider's own claim measures the trip against the wrong baseline. This was a RYDE_POOL trip, and under POL-RD-12 the baseline for the POL-RD-01 threshold test is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km (16.0 km), not the solo-rider figure the rider quotes (trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km = 11.5 km). The rider's 16.0 km comparison is the correct one; the 11.5 km figure is carried for reference only and a claim built on it fails on that ground alone.

On the correct pooled baseline the trace shows no deviation at all. The governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 16.96 km (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.0 km). Excess over the matched-itinerary optimal of 16.0 km is 0.96 km, or 6.00% — below both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute). The derived deviation block itself records status 'no deviation'.

The 0.96 km of excess is exactly the kind of distance POL-RD-12 excludes: distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. The trip record's optimal_route_source confirms the baseline was 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider', and the driver's counterparty statement says the same — the co-rider pickup is part of the itinerary. The rider's own claim text concedes the extra distance was 'picking up someone else'.

The rider's arithmetic on the fare is also wrong on its own terms. The fare breakdown shows charged_total of 23.51, of which 12.00 is distance charge and 6.16 time charge on a METERED model; the rider's quoted '$23.51' is the total charged, not a distance overcharge. Because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available.

The rider's claim that the app 'says the matched route is 16.0 km' is consistent with the record and undercuts the claim: the platform's own matched-itinerary optimal for this pooled trip is 16.0 km, and the trace came in at 16.96 km — a 6% overrun, not the 39% the rider implies by comparing against the 11.5 km solo figure.

The driver's traffic explanation is not needed and is not relied on here, but the record is clean on the point: no traffic advisory covers this corridor (EV-ADVIS-02860-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0), so no POL-RD-03 exoneration is asserted. The case is decided on the trace and the pooled baseline alone.

The rider's profile does not assist the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant is not in play — but neither is there any pattern of substantiated claims to lend weight to this one. The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged limb (b): no excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold is shown on the correct pooled baseline.

The driver's profile is context only and is not cited as a ground of decision. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 185, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral is warranted. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (1) is a near-synonym trap and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for.

The GPS trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and no straight-line jump over 500 m. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met, so no corroboration requirement arises and the trace may be relied on directly.

The fare ledger reconciles and carries no phantom lines: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00, and the ledger lines reconcile to total_charged of 23.51. No billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) is available to the rider, and no POL-RD-10(8) escalation trigger fires.

The chat log is empty (0 messages), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is asserted and none is needed. The absence of any chat instruction is consistent with the pooled-itinerary explanation: the co-rider pickup was platform-matched, not rider-requested.

The rider's claim that the driver 'drove 16.96 km picking up someone else' is factually correct but legally irrelevant: on a RYDE_POOL trip the matched-itinerary optimal already includes the co-rider leg, and the trace exceeds that matched baseline by only 0.96 km — inside the POL-RD-01 tolerance. The claim should be dismissed and the present payment state left as it is.

claims.text: The rider's claim measures the trip against the wrong baseline. This was a RYDE_POOL trip, and under POL-RD-12 the baseline for the POL-RD-01 threshold test is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km (16.0 km), not the solo-rider figure of 11.5 km carried separately as trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km for reference only. A claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone.

On the correct pooled baseline the measured excess is 0.96 km, which is 6.00% of the 16.0 km matched-itinerary optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceed 0.8 km absolute. The percentage test fails by a wide margin (6.00% against 20%), so no route deviation is established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 16.96 km against a 16.0 km matched-itinerary optimal, an excess of 0.96 km — the same sub-threshold figure the derived deviation block reports.

The distance the rider complains about — the co-rider pickup — is expressly excluded from excess. POL-RD-12 provides that distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation and is excluded from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trip_record's optimal_route_source confirms the matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider, and the driver's counterparty statement says the same.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes and carries the finding without discount. It has 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds — well inside the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment thresholds of a 90-second gap, a 500 m jump or a sustained interval above 30 seconds. The admissibility pre-pass likewise tags it COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The rider's own profile does not support the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger for a sub-30% excess is not engaged — but equally there is no history of substantiated deviation claims on this account to lend the present claim weight.

No driver-side pattern can be used against the driver here, and none should be. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is triggered only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation; no deviation at all is established on this trace, so the clause is not engaged. For completeness, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 185 completed_trips_90d, which is far below the 3-flag or 0.05-ratio pattern threshold.

The fare was billed on the metered model and the rider was charged 23.51 SGD, with no refund issued and the charge still standing. Because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. NO_ACTION leaves the present payment state as it is, which on this rider-filed dispute means the charge stands.

No billing-integrity correction is owed either. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied airport surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's contested amount of 1.50 SGD has no line of the fare_breakdown behind it.

The driver's traffic position is not needed and is not relied on. No traffic_advisory covers this corridor — EV-ADVIS-02860-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record. That is immaterial to this ruling: the deviation fails the POL-RD-01 threshold on the trace itself, before any exculpatory clause is reached, so the absent advisory neither helps nor hurts the driver.

The chat log is empty — zero messages, no first or last message timestamp — so no rider instruction of any kind is recorded for this trip. POL-RD-04's rider-requested-detour exoneration cannot be invoked, and equally no rider instruction exists that could have caused the measured excess. The claim rests on the trace and the trip record alone.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties, in plain language.

This was a pooled ride (RYDE_POOL, trip TRP-02860), and that fixes the baseline the distance is measured against. Under POL-RD-12 the comparison figure is the matched-itinerary optimal on the trip record, trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km. The rider's 11.5 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried for reference only; POL-RD-12 says a claim built on it has cited the wrong field, and this one does.

The governing actual distance is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record. POL-RD-01 says gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test. EV-GPS-02860 records 16.96 km; the trip record's 17.0 km is a convenience copy. Excess = 16.96 − 16.0 = 0.96 km, which is 6.00% of the optimal, matching the derived deviation block (derived.deviation.excess_km 0.96, excess_pct 6.00, status "no deviation").

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The 0.96 km does clear the absolute 0.8 km limb, but 6.00% is far below the 20% limb (which would need about 3.2 km). Because both must pass, no route deviation is established. The distance the rider noticed — picking up the co-rider — is in any event excluded from excess by POL-RD-12, since the trip record's optimal_route_source confirms a matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider and the driver's statement says the same; but the case does not need to reach that point.

The trace also carries the finding without discount. It is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, no straight-line jump over 500 m. No corroboration requirement arises and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation fires.

On billing, the fare ledger reconciles to charged_total 23.51 (base fare 3.80 + distance charge 12.75 + time charge 6.16 + platform fee 0.80), with zero ERP gantries, zero tolls and zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09(4) therefore has no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge to refund, and the rider's contested 1.50 SGD corresponds to no line of the fare breakdown. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available.

The driver's traffic explanation was not needed to decide this case and is not relied on. No traffic advisory covers the corridor — EV-ADVIS-02860-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 could not have been run; two claims that raised this without naming the impairment were discarded by the referee and are listed below. The absence neither helps nor hurts the driver here, because the claim fails the POL-RD-01 threshold on the trace itself.

The profile arguments change nothing. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger is not engaged. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 185 completed_trips_90d, far below POL-RD-06's pattern test (3 flags, or a 0.05 ratio), so no repeat-deviation pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used as a ground by either side.

The charge was METERED and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. NO_ACTION leaves that state as it is: on this rider-filed dispute the charge stands, no refund is due to the rider and no compensation is due to the driver. As the monetary effect is zero, well under the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, no amount is held. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-02860, a RYDE_POOL (pooled) trip for which SGD 23.51 was charged. The rider says the trip should be measured against an 11.5 km route and that 16.96 km was driven to collect someone else. The claim is not supported by the evidence, and the present payment state stands (NO_ACTION).

Baseline (POL-RD-12). On a pooled trip the POL-RD-01 threshold is measured against the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km (EV-TRIP-02860), not against trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km = 11.5 km, which is carried for reference only. The rider's comparison to 11.5 km cites the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched itinerary is excluded from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied, and the trip record's optimal_route_source confirms the 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'.

Threshold (POL-RD-01). The governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 16.96 km (EV-GPS-02860); POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km = 17.0 km. Excess = 16.96 - 16.0 = 0.96 km, i.e. 6.00% of the 16.0 km optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass: excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The percentage test fails (6.00% against 20%), so no route deviation is established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 133 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s, no jump over 500 m. Limbs (a) to (c) are not met, so no corroboration requirement arises and the trace carries the finding undiscounted. It is the deciding artifact, together with the trip record, both at weight 1.0.

Fare (POL-RD-02, POL-RD-09). Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. The fare ledger reconciles to charged_total of 23.51 (base 3.80 + distance 12.75 + time 6.16 + platform fee 0.80); the rider's quoted '$23.51' is the total charged, not a distance overcharge, and the contested 1.50 SGD has no line of the fare breakdown behind it. There are zero ERP lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) is owed and POL-RD-10(8) does not fire.

Other clauses. EV-CHAT-02860 is empty (0 messages), so no rider instruction exists and POL-RD-04 cannot be invoked. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no MATERIAL deviation, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 185 shows no pattern (the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field the clause names and was not used). rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d = 0 does not assist the rider's claim.

Missing artifact. EV-ADVIS-02860-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; it can carry no fact. No party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and POL-RD-13 is not engaged, and the absent advisory neither helps nor hurts the driver. The two claims that cited it were discarded at the mechanical check for citing an impaired artifact without disclosing its issue code.

The driver's counterparty statement (pooled ride, co-rider pickup part of the itinerary) is consistent with the trip record but is not needed to decide the case; the pooled baseline is established by the trip record itself.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; timestamps do not conflict or run backwards; the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or deficient artifact; no phantom charge line exists; and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. No referral is produced: POL-RD-06(c) requires a MATERIAL substantiated deviation and POL-RD-09(4) requires an unmatched charge line, and neither condition holds. The monetary effect is nil, which is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so nothing is held and the charge stands as billed.

The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied airport surcharge to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's contested amount of 1.50 SGD has no line of the fare_breakdown behind it.

The driver's traffic position is not needed and is not relied on. No traffic_advisory covers this corridor — EV-ADVIS-02860-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record. That is immaterial to this ruling: the deviation fails the POL-RD-01 threshold on the trace itself, before any exculpatory clause is reached, so the absent advisory neither helps nor hurts the driver.

ledger.claim: The chat log is empty — zero messages, no first or last message timestamp — so no rider instruction of any kind is recorded for this trip. POL-RD-04's rider-requested-detour exoneration cannot be invoked, and equally no rider instruction exists that could have caused the measured excess. The claim rests on the trace and the trip record alone.
